increment_paragraph: **ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN** (discharging ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN; [report](../../reports/arm-obligations-unit-grain/README.md)) narrows the carriage of a rule package admission's obligations from the unit to the rows whose derivation rests on it. The unit frame now attributes what it carries (`arm_obligations::FrameCarriage`): rule 37's checked-specification admissions to their specification (`legacy_checked_spec::Settled::carried` is per specification), everything else (a host's admission, a nested frame's hand-up) to the unit, as before. A row carries the unit's obligations and those of every declaration it reaches: itself, or a name its work's body spells (minted spellings read back), its row's applied callees or its relied-on callback candidates name, closed over every in-unit function with work in the frame (`contract_dependencies::attribution::reaching`). The notes are taken by `within`, `body` and the new `contract_dependencies::relied` while a frame is open, in every run, never from the audit's rule 13f recording, so the certificate recheck (which reruns outside that recording and compares the program summary) reproduces each row's carriage; rule 13f's text names this one reader. A differential rerun was rejected because W4's validation of the asserting body would let callers shed a premise their verdict still rests on (RULE37-W4-ASSERT-PREMISE-VISIBILITY). Tests: a unit's transitive callers of the admitted declaration carry it and an unrelated row does not, an open obligation keeps exactly those rows `Unknown`, unit-grain obligations still reach every row, nested frames hand up at unit grain, the closure follows callees, relied candidates, minted spellings and unbodied work, and rows are identical with a recording open; `tests/rule37_switch.rs` adds a transitive caller (carries) and an unrelated function (carries nothing) to the provider fixture, and its `Safe` certificate rechecks. Lean `QCore.ArmObligations` gains 11 audited theorems (row grain refines unit grain, holds every obligation the derivation used under the record's completeness, transitive-callee and nested cases, unknown attribution is the unit grain, a `Safe` row rests on no open obligation). Measurement (`quirin-audit measure --declared`, `rev:3e53c34fe` -> `rev:051aef7f2`, three live profiles; `baseline:98b1bb785` was refused because its route definitions predate 3e53c34fe's link-map move): no verdict moves on any route; on the corpus 789 of the 2,693 rows that carried `asserted_allocation` keep it (34 Safe, 752 Unknown, 3 Unsafe) and 1,904 drop it (394 Safe, 1,508 Unknown, 2 Unsafe), every one of the 54 units keeping at least one carrying row, each dropped row's assumptions digest returning to its sources digest; every row whose rule 13f dependencies name `rd_calloc` or `rd_strdup` (271) still carries it. Card gate on `051aef7f2`: Rust 8,945 passed / 0 failed, Lean 1 audit, Python 568 tests.
status_paragraph: Rule-package obligations are carried at row grain where attributed (ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN, measured `rev:3e53c34fe` -> `rev:051aef7f2`, no verdict moved on any route): on the corpus 789 rows (34 Safe, 752 Unknown, 3 Unsafe) of the 54 librdkafka units in which `rd_calloc` or `rd_strdup` stands as a checked specification carry rule 37's `asserted_allocation`, the rows whose derivation reaches either specification; the other 1,904 rows of those units no longer list it. System and slice carry none.

ledger.why: DISCHARGE (ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN, 2026-11-01): the unit frame attributes its obligations (arm_obligations::FrameCarriage). Rule 37's checked-specification admissions are carried only by the rows whose derivation reaches the specification (the row itself; a name its body spells, its row's applied callees or its relied-on callback candidates name; transitively through every in-unit function with work in the frame), computed from per-frame notes taken in every run (contract_dependencies::attribution), never from the audit's recording, so the certificate recheck reproduces it. Admissions without an established attribution (hosts, nested frames' hand-ups) keep the unit grain. Tests: tests/unit/arm_obligations.rs (transitive callers carry, an unrelated row does not, an open obligation keeps exactly the resting rows Unknown, nested frames hand up at unit grain, the closure's sources, recording independence) and tests/rule37_switch.rs (provider fixture with a transitive caller and an unrelated function, Safe certificate recheck). Lean QCore.ArmObligations: row grain refines unit grain and holds every obligation the derivation used. Measured: corpus 789 of 2,693 carrying rows keep asserted_allocation, 1,904 drop it, no verdict moved.

ledger.text: ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN: this residual is why the row grain is attributed by consultation, not by a rerun with the admission refused: with the specification withdrawn, W4 validates the same non-null result from the asserting body, so a differential rerun would let callers shed asserted_allocation while their verdict still rests on the deployed-build fact.

ledger.title: A host's admission obligations are still carried at unit grain
ledger.text: ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN attributes only admissions of a named declaration (rule 37's checked-specification settlement) to rows. An admission asked through arm_obligations::consult at a host position (rules 33 to 36's hosts, the route table's fallbacks, RULE32A-PILOT's caller-frame hold host) and a nested analysis's carriage handed to the enclosing frame are carried by every row of the unit, because which rows read that lowering is not attributed (a lowering computed inside one function's work may be reused by a whole-unit pass). No such host returns an obligation today, so no live row is affected. DISCHARGE: when a host package first returns an obligation, attribute it to the function scopes whose work asked (contract_dependencies' active stack) with a census showing the lowering is not reused outside that work, plus a test, or record unit grain as the intended precision for that host.

ledger.title: The row-grain attribution's wall-time cost is unmeasured
ledger.text: ARM-OBLIGATIONS-UNIT-GRAIN notes every function's work and body in the unit frame's attribution in every run (contract_dependencies::within and body now open their scope whenever a frame is open, not only under the audit's recording) and computes a reach closure for units with an attributed admission. In its measurement the TIP corpus route (rev:051aef7f2) took 2 h 25 min and the BASE one (rev:3e53c34fe) 1 h 53 min, each measured once, in different measure runs, under different host load, so the difference is unattributed. Runs without a recording (unit tests, the certificate recheck) now open per-function consultation logs too. DISCHARGE: interleaved wall-time medians of BASE and TIP on the corpus route (or the analysis of the 54 carrying units alone), and an optimisation if the attribution costs measurably, or a record that it does not.
